content.user_title: Build Production LLM Apps and AI Agents
content.value_statement: Teams need reliable LLM systems that handle retrieval, orchestration, safety, and cost. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through production AI design and implementation.
actual_capabilities: Designs production LLM application architectures with model routing and fallback strategies.
Plans RAG systems with chunking, embeddings, vector databases, hybrid search, and reranking.
Guides AI agent workflows using tool integration, memory, orchestration, and evaluation.
Adds safety controls for prompt injection, PII handling, moderation, and compliance.
Recommends observability, testing, caching, rate limits, and cost controls for AI services.
Supports multimodal AI planning for documents, images, audio, and cross-modal retrieval.
limitations: It provides guidance and implementation patterns, but it does not host models or services.
It requires project data, deployment targets, and business constraints for precise architecture choices.
It cannot guarantee model behavior without evaluation, monitoring, and staged rollout.
It may need current provider documentation for rapidly changing model capabilities.

use_cases.title: Launch an Enterprise RAG Assistant
use_cases.description: Plan ingestion, chunking, embeddings, retrieval, reranking, access control, and evaluation for a knowledge assistant.

use_cases.title: Build a Tool-Using Support Agent
use_cases.description: Design agent workflows with memory, tools, escalation logic, monitoring, and safety checks for customer operations.

use_cases.title: Harden an Existing LLM Feature
use_cases.description: Review prompts, retrieval quality, abuse cases, PII handling, latency, cost, and production observability.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic LLM Feature
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a new AI feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a simple LLM feature for my app. Include data flow, model choice, prompt structure, tests, and rollout steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a RAG Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a RAG pipeline for these documents and users. Cover ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector storage, retrieval, reranking, and evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Implement an Agent Workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for multi-step AI automation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an agent architecture with tools, memory, permissions, escalation paths, observability, safety checks, and failure handling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Production AI Reliability
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert request for a deployed or near-release system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this LLM system for reliability, security, cost, latency, monitoring, prompt injection risk, PII handling, and release readiness.

output_examples.input: Design a RAG assistant for internal policy documents.
output: Architecture covering ingestion, chunking, vector storage, hybrid retrieval, reranking, answer generation, and source citation.
Evaluation plan with golden questions, retrieval metrics, hallucination checks, access control tests, and monitoring requirements.

output_examples.input: Improve a chatbot that is slow and expensive.
output: Optimization plan using model routing, response caching, streaming, prompt trimming, rate limits, and fallback behavior.
Operational checks for latency budgets, cost alerts, error tracking, and staged rollout.

output_examples.input: Add safety controls to an AI agent.
output: Safety design with tool permissions, prompt injection checks, PII redaction, audit logs, escalation rules, and adversarial tests.
Release checklist for monitoring, incident response, policy review, and human override paths.

best_practices: Provide data sources, user roles, latency targets, cost limits, and compliance needs before requesting architecture.
Ask for evaluation metrics and rollout stages with every production AI implementation.
Review safety, observability, and fallback behavior before exposing tools or sensitive data.
anti_patterns: Do not ship LLM features without tests for retrieval quality, prompt injection, and failure cases.
Do not expose agents to powerful tools without permissions, audit logs, and human escalation.
Do not choose models only by benchmark scores without checking latency, cost, context, and policy needs.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build LLM applications, RAG systems, AI agents, multimodal workflows, and production AI infrastructure.

faq.question: Can it choose models for my project?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare model options using capability, latency, cost, context size, tool support, and deployment constraints.

faq.question: Does it support enterprise RAG systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers ingestion, embeddings, vector databases, hybrid search, reranking, evaluation, access control, and monitoring.

faq.question: Can it improve AI safety?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends controls for prompt injection, PII, moderation, bias, tool permissions, and incident response.

faq.question: Does it replace provider documentation?
faq.answer: No. Provider APIs and model capabilities change often, so current documentation should confirm implementation details.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Engineers, architects, and product teams building production AI features with Claude, Codex, Claude Code, or similar tools.
